previous.title: Insecure direct object reference (IDOR) in controlled lab

cvssDetails.reason: Score derived from observed impact/exploitability assumptions; verify against the final authorized deployment context.

previous.description: A synthetic object endpoint returned another synthetic user object without an ownership check.
previous.impact: Cross-user object access would expose or alter records if the same authorization flaw existed in production.
previous.remediation: Enforce object ownership/tenant authorization on every object lookup; return 403 for unauthorized IDs; retest the identical request.
steps: Request object_id=2 without an authorized owner context.

poc.expected: 403 Forbidden for an object not owned by caller

previous.title: Reflected XSS output encoding failure in controlled lab

cvssDetails.reason: Score derived from observed impact/exploitability assumptions; verify against the final authorized deployment context.

previous.description: A synthetic query value was reflected into an HTML field without output encoding.
previous.impact: A production equivalent could execute attacker-controlled script in another user’s browser and access browser-visible application data.
previous.remediation: Contextually encode untrusted output before HTML insertion; use a restrictive CSP as defense in depth; retest the same payload.
steps: Submit a benign script marker in q.

previous.title: JWT algorithm confusion (alg:none) in controlled lab

cvssDetails.reason: Score derived from observed impact/exploitability assumptions; verify against the final authorized deployment context.

previous.description: A synthetic JWT verification endpoint accepted an unsigned token and granted an admin role marker.
previous.evidence: 200 unsigned JWT accepted with admin marker
previous.impact: A production equivalent could allow privilege escalation where JWT signatures are not enforced.
previous.remediation: Pin accepted algorithms server-side, require a valid signature and key, validate issuer/audience/expiry, and reject alg:none; retest the same token condition.
steps: Submit the synthetic unsigned JWT condition.

poc.actual: 200 unsigned JWT accepted with admin marker

previous.title: SSRF destination validation failure in controlled lab

cvssDetails.reason: Score derived from observed impact/exploitability assumptions; verify against the final authorized deployment context.

previous.description: A synthetic fetch endpoint accepted a loopback destination without allowlisting or network-boundary validation.
previous.impact: A production equivalent could allow access to internal services or metadata endpoints.
previous.remediation: Use an explicit destination allowlist, resolve and validate IPs after DNS, block loopback/private/link-local ranges, and apply egress network controls.
steps: Submit a loopback URL to the synthetic fetch endpoint.

previous.title: Missing baseline security headers in the SentinelScan local development server

cvssDetails.reason: Score derived from observed impact/exploitability assumptions; verify against the final authorized deployment context.

previous.description: The SentinelScan local development server does not emit one or more recommended browser security headers. This is a local development hardening finding, not evidence that World Monitor production is vulnerable.
previous.affected: SentinelScan local development server · GET / response headers
previous.impact: Missing browser security headers can reduce defense in depth against content injection, framing and unwanted browser behavior if an application-layer flaw is later introduced.
previous.remediation: Add a reviewed Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, a restrictive Referrer-Policy and an appropriate Permissions-Policy; validate the policy in staging and retest the response headers.
steps: Record each missing header and retest after configuration changes.

poc.expected: CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy as applicable
